primary_claim: The length of tasks (measured by human completion time) that frontier AI agents can complete autonomously with 50% reliability has been doubling approximately every 7 months for the past 6 years, with current best models such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet having roughly a one-hour time horizon.

effect.value: approximately every 7 months over the last 6 years; Claude 3.7 Sonnet has a time horizon of roughly one hour; SWE-Bench Verified replication shows an even faster doubling time of under 3 months

contradicts_or_qualifies: helps resolve the apparent contradiction between superhuman AI performance on many benchmarks and the common observation that models are not robustly helpful in automating day-to-day work: current best models can do some tasks that take expert humans hours, but only reliably complete tasks up to a few minutes long
stated_future_work: replications or extensions of this work by others, which would be highly informative for forecasting the real-world impacts of AI
limitations_stated: the estimate of task length an agent can complete depends on methodological choices like the tasks used and the humans whose performance is measured
there remains the possibility of substantial model error; fitting the trend to only 2024-2025 data shortens the estimated arrival of 50%-reliable month-long task completion by about 2.5 years
the SWE-Bench Verified replication's faster doubling time may be partly explained by how human time estimates are operationalized (excluding codebase familiarization time)
the sensitivity analysis does not account for future changes in the trend or external validity concerns, which are responsible for the majority of the uncertainty
quote: We show that this metric has been consistently exponentially increasing over the past 6 years, with a doubling time of around 7 months.
